title: Morning infra bulletboard
content:
Quick morning brain dump and running list — keep this clipped and actionable.

Context: hands-on shift today. Focus = keep Dedicated pools healthy, watch token surge from internal load-test (campaign B), and finish the small netfix for node label drift.

Top priorities (order matters):
- [ ] Stabilize p-pool-03 (eu-west-1-d). Observed 4x enqueue latency spikes starting ~02:30 UTC. Check pod restarts + kube-scheduler logs. Suspect preemptions interacting with autoscaler config.
- [ ] Drain and reprovision node g3-88 (reported high GPU mem fragmentation). Schedule drain during low traffic window (15m window: 10:30–10:45 UTC).
- [ ] Patch node-label-sync job to ignore ephemeral labels (PR ready, needs +1 from Samir). If merged, kick a rolling restart for label-sync deployment.
- [ ] Confirm fallback routing for hosted-api route /v1/generate — ensure can still fallback to small-quant models if pool saturates. Test with synthetic requests.

Short checklist / commands to run now:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --label-columns=gpu_type,pool
- kubectl describe pod p-pool-03-*-runner | egrep -i "OOM|terminated|preempt"
- aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:pool,Values=p-pool-03" --region eu-west-1 | jq '.Reservations[].Instances[] | {InstanceId,State,InstanceType,Tags}'
- curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY' https://api.redwood.test/v1/status/pool/p-pool-03 | jq

Observations from last night (hand-off notes):
- Load test started at 23:45 UTC, ramp to 350 rps. Token burn clipped at 10M tokens/hr. p-pool-03 hit 95% memory across g3 nodes but CPU still low.
- Autoscaler did not trigger new nodes — scale policy uses average GPU mem free < 12% threshold; current mem pattern is spiky which confuses scale window.
- Two transient preemptions logged from spot provider between 02:20–02:35. k8s recorded graceful shutdowns but model warmups did not finish before requests arrived => latency spikes.

Notes / hypotheses:
- Shorten the autoscaler evaluation window for p-pool-* to 30s for the next 6h to test responsiveness during the load test. Risk: more churn. Add a guard to block scale-down while active jobs > 5.
- If mem fragmentation is the core issue, try a node re-provision with newer cuda driver + patch kernel flags we tested on staging (patch id: qc-kern-smooth-2026). Could reduce fragmentation.

Quick troubleshooting script sketch (for manual run):
1) curl pool status endpoint -> parse node list
2) ssh to candidate node -> sudo nvidia-smi -q | grep -A6 "FB Memory"
3) if fragmentation > 60% -> cordon + drain -> reprovision instance with image g3-2026-stable
4) verify model warmup by hitting /v1/health/warmup endpoint until 200

User impact/SLAs to watch:
- Hosted API for customers in eu-west-1: 99.9% latency SLO for /v1/generate. If p-pool-03 continues to misbehave for >15m, open incident and flip routing to backup pool p-pool-01 (manual for now).
- Internal regression: load-test campaign B is pushing new prompt patterns with long prompt prefixes; caching pressure high. Might need KV cache TTL bump.

Follow-ups and handoff notes to leave in incident channel:
- Attach the autoscaler metrics for the 02:00–03:00 window (graph in PRD: INFRA-2147).
- Add a short blurb to the incident timeline about preemption pattern.

Loose todos (not blocking shift but OK to start):
- [ ] Draft a tiny runbook section for "warmup timeout" and add to console runbooks (link => Confluence pending).
- [ ] Add e2e test that simulates spot preemption and verifies fallback routing in the CI harness.
- [ ] Coordinate with network team to double-check SG rules for p-pool-03 instances (Samir to help).

Questions to resolve by EOD:
- Does the autoscaler history show repeated scale-up/scale-down flips (thrashing) over the last 7 days? If yes, we should tune hysteresis.
- Is the spot provider policy for eu-west-1 different for g3 family? (Might be causing sudden preemptions).

Quick links / anchors to reference during shift:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/486 (node-label fix)
- JIRA: INFRA-2147 (p-pool-03 persistent latency)
- Staging runbook: confluence.redwood/infra/pool-warmup (draft)

Random notes to self (brain dump):
- If we end up reprovisioning, leave a short note to compute-team about cost hit — include estimate: +1 large instance ~ $0.85/hr in eu-west-1.
- For the KV cache TTL: quick test values = 45s, 120s. Start with 45s and watch hit ratio for 20m.

End-of-shift handover template (fill and paste to #infra-ops):
- What I did: (list)
- What I saw: (metrics + links)
- What I changed: (commands/PRs)
- What next: (open tasks, owners)

If anything gets hairy, ping Mira (oncall) and drop a short note with timestamps and the grafana link.

-- zara
